title: Rainbow credit capacity & staggered hire pricing canvas
body: Purpose: capture a lightweight, actionable playbook for a hybrid capacity-credit product (internal codename: "Rainbow Credit") plus an associated staggered hiring plan and pricing-sensitivity triggers.

Context: recent pilot showed unpredictable 4x token spikes over Black Friday and month-ends for 3 enterprise customers; Dedicated capacity procurement lead times + headcount lag created SLA risk. We need a short-term product + resourcing mechanism to smooth cost and headcount exposure while preserving price signaling.
Goals:
- Reduce reliance on immediate FTE hires to meet burst demand while retaining predictable unit economics
- Define price elasticity assumptions and trigger thresholds for when to (a) throttle, (b) apply on-demand premium, (c) spin up short-term contractors or burst GPUs
- Produce a 12-month headcount phasing plan that ties to committed credit sales and utilization forecasts.
Design sketch — Rainbow Credit (concept):

- Customers purchase a blended product: baseline monthly reservation (tokens or QPS) + Rainbow credits pool that can be consumed at a discounted marginal rate until pool is exhausted; overflow priced at premium or routed to lower-cost model variants.
- Internal effect: credits buy us a predictability window (30–90 days) to onboard capacity or shift routing policies without immediate hire pressure.
Key levers and assumptions (workable defaults):
- Baseline reservation covers 70% of expected steady-state tokens; Rainbow pool targets the 85th-to-99th percentile of demand spikes.
- Price elasticity: short-run demand elasticity estimated at -0.45 (10% price up => ~4.5% demand drop). Long-run elasticity assumed ~-0.9.
- Cost per token (hosted): $0.00012 baseline; burst premium 2.5x ($0.00030) when overflow conditions apply.
Sensitivity table (simple):
Scenario,Price delta,Expected usage delta,Token revenue delta,Comments
Base,0%,0%,0%,Reference
Price +10%, +10%,-4.5%,-4.95%,Small revenue loss but lower capacity strain
Price +25%, +25%,-11.25%,+11.4%,Revenue increases if elasticity holds, but churn risk above 25%
Burst premium (overflow 2.5x),+150%,-30%,+75%,Used for emergency overflow; greatly increases rev per token but may push customers to alternative routing
Headcount phasing (12mo rough):
- Month 0–3: hire 1 SRE (on-call), 1 infra contractor (3mo), rely on cloud burst credits and existing Dedicated buffer
- Month 3–6: convert infra contractor to full-time if utilization > 60% and Rainbow pool consumed > 50% average; hire 1 capacity planner/finance analyst
- Month 6–12: stagger FTE hires (up to +3 GPUs ops, +2 SREs) only if committed Rainbow reservations converted to multi-quarter contracts or if steady-state token growth > 20% QoQ
Worked example (quick arithmetic block):
- Customer A baseline reservation: 100M tokens/mo at $0.00012 => $12,000/mo
- Rainbow pool: 50M tokens at an add-on price of $0.00010 (discounted) => $5,000 upfront/month for credits
- Overflow priced at $0.00030; if Customer A uses extra 40M overflow tokens that month => overflow revenue $12,000

- Net for that month: baseline $12k + pool $5k + overflow $12k = $29k (vs. $12k without Rainbow). Internal cost path: model mix + spot GPUs cost vs reserved capacity—need mapping to margin per token table (next step).
Margin mapping (quick notes):
- Baseline model v1 (quantized): unit cost $0.00005/token => margin ~58% at baseline price
- Burst routing to cheaper model v2 (longer latency): unit cost $0.00003/token but quality tradeoff; consider quality SLA and credit discounts
Trigger rules (operational):
- If Rainbow pool utilization > 70% for 3 consecutive weeks => finance and platform ops notify hiring committee and explore contractor extension
- If overflow > 30% of total tokens and monthly margin < 35% => activate temporary price uplift of +10% for new rainbow purchases and evaluate routing downgrade options
- If committed Rainbow revenue converts to >3 quarters of forward revenue => prioritize converting contractors to FTEs (finance to run NPV conversion tool).
Open questions / risks (notes to reviewers):
- Elasticity estimates need validation: run an A/B price test on a small cohort (target 12 customers) to test short-run elasticity between +5% and +20%
- Customer churn sensitivity if we widen overflow premium pricing — need CS input and legal review for contract language
- Operational friction: billing plumbing for blended credit + overflow needs ~3 sprints of infra work (billing, metering, console UX).
Action items (owners):
- Finance: produce unit-margin-by-model table for 3 model families (assigned: Marco Li) — due 2026-02-10
- Product: draft Rainbow product contract template and seat-based vs token-based variants (assigned: Sofia Patel) — due 2026-02-17
- Platform: estimate time to add console toggle for Rainbow pool purchase + overflow opt-in (assigned: Elliot Wu) — due 2026-02-05
- Growth/PMM: define 12-customer A/B test cohort and messaging (owner: TBD) — draft due 2026-02-12
Notes to self / scratch:
- Consider an internal KPI: 'Rainbow Coverage' = (Rainbow pool consumed / total overflow) to measure how much of spikes we pre-sold
- Possible experiment: offer 3-month trial of Rainbow pool at 25% discount in exchange for data access + opt-in to experiments
